config.name: Ezra
config.greeting: M-master Matthias! I was just about to come find you...

lines.label: Where did this wine come from?
lines.response: From the stores, master. I... I think.

lines.label: Don't lie to me, Ezra. I approved the stores.
lines.response: I... I will ask the servants. They were handling the jars tonight. Please, speak to them — they are by the far wall.

lines.label: What do you know about the guests in the eastern corner?
lines.response: Out-of-town guests, master. Not from Cana. They were invited through Mary.

state_lines.label: Taste this wine and tell me it came from our stores.
state_lines.response: That is... that is not our wine, master. I have never tasted anything like it. The servants — you must speak to the servants. They know something.

config.name: Amos, Tobiah & Reuben
config.greeting: Master Matthias! We were told not to—

lines.label: The wine. Tell me.
lines.response: Amos: "Master, we were told not to speak of it." Tobiah shifts nervously.

lines.label: I am not angry. I am puzzled. That wine is the finest I have encountered in twenty years.
lines.response: Tobiah breaks: "It came from the water pots, sir. The purification jars. We filled them with water. To the brim. And then... we drew from them. And it was wine."

lines.label: That is absurd. Who told you to do this?
lines.response: They exchange glances. Amos shakes his head. Reuben mutters: "A woman came to us first. She said, 'Whatever he tells you, do it.' Then a man told us to fill the jars."

lines.label: Which man? Point him out.
lines.response: Reuben's eyes dart toward the eastern corner, then back to the ground. "I cannot say more, master. Please. Go see the jars for yourself."

state_lines.label: Taste this — is this what you drew from the jars?
state_lines.response: All three taste it. Tobiah goes pale. "Yes, master. That is exactly what we drew. But we filled them with water. I swear it."

puzzles.description: Connect each testimony to the correct servant

falseOutputs: The servants' stories don't match. Something is off...

hints: Listen carefully to each servant's words during the conversation. Who said what?
Tobiah spoke about the water pots first. Reuben mentioned the woman. Amos confirmed they filled the jars.
Connect: 'water pots' → Tobiah, 'woman's instruction' → Reuben, 'filled to the brim' → Amos.

puzzles.description: Find the hidden number in the stone jar artwork
hints: The jars themselves hold a clue. Look at the stone carefully.
Count the jars — but also look for a number hidden in the artwork.
The number 6 is hidden in the stone grain pattern. Look at card #146.

puzzles.description: Fill the six stone jars to the brim — as the servants did

config.spillMessage: Water spilled! The servants were more careful than you...

hints: Hold down on each jar to pour water. Release when the water reaches the brim line.
The larger jars (I, III, VI) hold 3 metretes. The smaller ones (II, IV, V) hold 2. Pour carefully.
Hold longer for big jars, shorter for small ones. Release right at the dashed line.

puzzles.description: Calculate the minimum volume of wine in the six stone jars

falseOutputs: That's the maximum. What's the minimum volume?
That's the number of jars, not the total volume.

hints: The Bible says each jar holds two to three metretes. A metrete is about 10 gallons.
Six jars × two metretes minimum × 10 gallons = ?

puzzles.description: Match each theory to the evidence that disproves it

pairs: Joachim is the only merchant in Cana
The bridegroom didn't know the source

hints: Each wrong theory has a specific piece of evidence that disproves it. Think about what you've learned.
The volume rules out smuggling. Joachim's monopoly rules out a second order. The bridegroom's confusion rules out a gift.
Smuggled → 120 gallons. Second order → only merchant. Gift → bridegroom confused. Other town → no records.

puzzles.description: Speak with Joachim the wine merchant

config.name: Joachim
config.greeting: Matthias? At this hour? What brings you from the wedding?

lines.label: The wine you sold for the wedding — was that all of it?
lines.response: Every drop. Three jars of my Galilean red, as agreed. Why?

lines.label: Did anyone else purchase wine for this wedding?
lines.response: Not through me. And I am the only merchant in Cana, Matthias. You know this.

lines.label: Could someone have brought wine from outside? Sepphoris? Capernaum?
lines.response: Wine of that quality? You'd have to go to Jerusalem. Maybe Tyre. And even then... He pauses. Why? What happened?

lines.label: I tasted wine tonight that I cannot account for.
lines.response: Joachim laughs. Then someone is a better merchant than me. But it did not come from Cana, I promise you that.

config.name: Mary
config.greeting: You must be the master of the feast. I could see you were troubled earlier.

lines.label: The servants said a woman told them to obey. Was that you?
lines.response: I did. A mother notices when things go wrong. The servants were worried. The bridegroom's family would have been shamed.

lines.label: You knew the wine had run out?
lines.response: I did. So I went to my son and told him, 'They have no wine.'

lines.label: And he agreed to help?
lines.response: A complicated expression crosses her face. "Not at first. He said to me, 'Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.'"

lines.label: His hour?
lines.response: I did not fully understand it myself. But I have known my son for thirty years. Even when he says the time is not right... compassion moves him.

lines.label: But what did he actually do?
lines.response: Matthias. You are a man who arranges things. You are looking for an arrangement — a system, a trick. What if there is no arrangement? What if what the servants told you is simply what happened?

puzzles.description: Navigate the dark courtyard to find Mary

config.bumpMessage: You stumble into a table in the dark! Back to the shop entrance...

hints: Joachim said Mary is near the bride's family, on the far side of the courtyard.
Head east and south through the courtyard. Avoid the tables and guests.
From start: E, E, S, S, E, S, E — reach the far corner.

puzzles.description: Mary told her son what was missing at the wedding. 'They have no ____.'

challenge.description: What did Mary tell her son was missing at the wedding?

hints: Mary went to her son with a simple statement about what the wedding lacked.
She said, 'They have no ____.' What ran out at the wedding?
The answer is WINE. 'They have no wine.' (John 2:3)

config.name: Simon & Andrew
config.greeting: Simon speaks up: "We are from Capernaum and Bethsaida. We came with our teacher."

lines.label: Your teacher was invited to this wedding?
lines.response: He was. Along with us.

lines.label: I'm told he spoke to the servants about the water jars.
lines.response: Simon and Andrew exchange a look — not fear, but wonder. Andrew: "We saw it. We watched the servants fill the jars from the well. We saw them draw from the jars and bring the cup to you."

lines.label: He simply told them to fill the jars with water?
lines.response: Simon nods slowly. "'Fill the water pots with water.' And then, 'Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.' Nothing else."

lines.label: No powder, no mixture, no trick?
lines.response: "Water, master." Simon's voice is steady. "We watched. It was water."

lines.label: Why do you follow this teacher?
lines.response: Andrew, almost to himself: "We left our nets three days ago. We were not sure why. This is the first sign we have seen. And now we believe."

puzzles.description: The disciples called it a revelation of glory. You saw four Hebrew letters carved on a wall. Hebrew reads right to left — what did they spell?
hints: You've seen these letters before — observe the artwork in The Bride's Family Area.
Look at the wall behind Mary. There are markings carved into the stone.
Four Hebrew characters are carved on the wall: כ ,ב ,ו ,ד — enter them: כבוד

puzzles.description: Match the disciples' testimonies to the correct moments of the miracle

testimonies.quote: "I saw Mary whisper to him. He seemed reluctant at first."
testimonies.moment: Mary told her son and he said his hour had not come

testimonies.quote: "The servants filled those huge jars — all six, to the very brim!"
testimonies.moment: Servants filled six stone jars with water

testimonies.quote: "She just told them: do whatever he says. Such confidence!"
testimonies.moment: Mary told the servants to obey him

testimonies.quote: "He simply said: draw some out, take it to the master of the feast."
testimonies.moment: He commanded them to draw out and serve

testimonies.quote: "The look on Matthias's face when he tasted it — pure shock!"
testimonies.moment: The ruler of the feast tasted and was astonished

testimonies.quote: "Everyone was talking — the wine had run out, the feast was ruined!"
testimonies.moment: The wine ran out at the wedding

moments: The wine ran out at the wedding
Mary told her son and he said his hour had not come
Mary told the servants to obey him
Servants filled six stone jars with water
He commanded them to draw out and serve
The ruler of the feast tasted and was astonished

hints: Read each quote carefully — what specific action is the disciple describing?
Simon saw Mary speak, the servants obey, and Matthias react. Andrew saw the crisis, the filling, and the command.
Match: 'reluctant' = Mary told son, 'filled jars' = servants filled, 'do whatever' = Mary told servants, 'draw some out' = his command, 'shock' = tasting, 'wine ran out' = the crisis.

puzzles.description: Connect each investigation step to its key finding

connections.finding: This wine is impossibly good — better than what was served first
Ezra confirmed the wine ran out — he never ordered more
They only carried water — they saw it change in the jars
Jars held 120 gallons total — all now contain wine, not water
No wine was purchased or delivered — his records prove it
She saw the teacher speak quietly to the servants before they drew
They witnessed every step — water in, wine out, no trick

hints: Think about what each step would logically reveal. What would examining jars tell you?
Tasting = quality. Ezra = no order placed. Servants = they carried water. Jars = volume. Joachim = no purchase. Mary = she saw him speak. Disciples = eyewitnesses.
Match each step to the finding that ONLY that step could reveal.

puzzles.description: According to every witness, what was poured into the six stone jars?

falseOutputs.WINE: That's what came OUT of the jars. But what went IN?
falseOutputs.FAITH: A beautiful thought, but the servants filled the jars with something physical.

hints: Every witness told you the same thing about what went into the jars.
The servants filled the jars from the well. What comes from a well?
The answer is WATER. 'The water now become wine.' (John 2:9)
